questions.stem: A sperm cell has many mitochondria concentrated in its middle section. How does this adaptation relate to its function?

options.text: Mitochondria help the sperm cell divide rapidly
Mitochondria provide energy for the tail to swim towards the egg
Mitochondria store the genetic information
Mitochondria protect the sperm from the immune system

questions.explanation: The mitochondria in the middle section of a sperm cell carry out aerobic respiration to release energy (ATP). This energy powers the movement of the tail (flagellum), enabling the sperm to swim the long distance through the female reproductive system to reach and fertilise the egg.

questions.stem: Red blood cells have a biconcave disc shape and lack a nucleus. A patient has a condition where their red blood cells are spherical instead. What problem would this cause?

options.text: The cells would carry more oxygen than normal
The cells would have a reduced surface area to volume ratio, decreasing oxygen absorption
The cells would not be able to contain haemoglobin
The cells would become too large for capillaries

questions.explanation: The biconcave shape of red blood cells increases the surface area to volume ratio, allowing faster diffusion of oxygen into and out of the cell. Spherical cells have a lower surface area to volume ratio, so oxygen exchange would be less efficient, reducing oxygen delivery to tissues.

questions.stem: Root hair cells have long, thin extensions. A gardener notices that plants in waterlogged soil are wilting despite plenty of water. What might explain this?

options.text: The root hair cells are absorbing too much water
Waterlogged soil lacks oxygen, so root cells cannot respire to power active transport of minerals
The root hairs grow longer in waterlogged soil
Water moves out of the roots by osmosis

questions.explanation: Root hair cells need to carry out active transport to absorb mineral ions from the soil, which requires energy from aerobic respiration. Waterlogged soil has very little oxygen, so the root cells cannot respire aerobically, reducing mineral uptake. The roots may also be damaged, impairing water absorption.

questions.stem: Nerve cells (neurones) can be up to 1 metre long in humans. Why is this length an advantage?

options.text: Longer cells can store more energy
Signals can travel quickly over long distances without needing to pass between many cells
Longer cells can carry out more photosynthesis
Longer cells have more nuclei

questions.explanation: The long axon of a nerve cell allows electrical impulses to travel rapidly over long distances (e.g., from the spinal cord to the foot) without needing to cross many synapses between cells. Each synapse causes a small delay, so fewer synapses means faster signal transmission.

questions.stem: Palisade mesophyll cells are packed with chloroplasts and are found near the top surface of leaves. What would happen to a plant if these cells were located at the bottom of the leaf instead?

options.text: Photosynthesis would increase because more CO2 is available at the bottom
Photosynthesis would decrease because less light reaches the bottom of the leaf
There would be no change in photosynthesis rate
The plant would absorb more water

questions.explanation: Palisade cells are positioned near the upper surface of the leaf to absorb maximum light for photosynthesis. If they were at the bottom, light would need to pass through several other cell layers first, reducing the light intensity reaching the chloroplasts and decreasing the rate of photosynthesis.
